stem: A 10-year-old develops ear pain after frequent water exposure. Which examination finding most strongly supports acute otitis externa rather than middle-ear disease?

options.text: Tenderness when the tragus is pressed
Bubbling and air-fluid levels behind the tympanic membrane
A full or bulging tympanic membrane
Purulent otorrhoea after tympanic membrane perforation
Ear pulling as the only sign in an infant

explanation: Acute otitis externa is suggested by tragal tenderness. This pain on pressing the tragus is a classic examination finding of external ear canal inflammation and helps distinguish it from middle-ear disease.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because tenderness when the tragus is pressed is a classic sign of acute otitis externa.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because bubbling and air-fluid levels behind the tympanic membrane suggest middle-ear pathology, such as otitis media with effusion.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a full or bulging tympanic membrane is more consistent with acute otitis media.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because purulent otorrhoea after tympanic membrane perforation is more in keeping with acute otitis media.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because ear pulling in an infant is a nonspecific sign of ear discomfort and is not the key finding for otitis externa.
